cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt and Canaan. God says, "You must not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you." (Leviticus 18:3) One land is behind them and one is ahead of them, and neither one is the pattern. Two lands, friends, one answer.

The answer is False. God doesn't say, "Go find a middle road." He says, "You are to practice My judgments and keep My statutes by walking in them. I am the LORD your God." (Leviticus 18:4) Israel's way is God's way, friends, start to finish. Nobody has to invent anything.

The reason is that the man who does them will live by them. God says, "Keep My statutes and My judgments, for the man who does these things will live by them. I am the LORD." (Leviticus 18:5) The reason isn't applause or scared enemies, friends. It's life. And He puts His name on it at the end.

The answer is nations. God says, "…by all these things the nations I am driving out before you have defiled themselves." (Leviticus 18:24) So He's pointing to the nations already in the land, friends. He's the One driving them out, too.

The land will vomit them out, and it's a blunt one, friends. God says, "Even the land has become defiled, so I am punishing it for its sin, and the land will vomit out its inhabitants." (Leviticus 18:25) I think this is a heavy picture. The land itself is part of this, and it is the land that does the vomiting out.

The answer is True. God says, "…you must not commit any of these abominations—neither your native-born nor the foreigner who lives among you." (Leviticus 18:26) The native-born and the foreigner living among them are both named, friends. Nobody gets a different rulebook.

The answer is False. God says, "So if you defile the land, it will vomit you out as it spewed out the nations before you." (Leviticus 18:28) Getting in the door doesn't mean you can do anything inside, friends. The same thing that happened to them could happen to Israel.

The answer is that he must be cut off from his people. God says, "Therefore anyone who commits any of these abominations must be cut off from among his people." (Leviticus 18:29) It's a serious line, friends, and I think it's meant to be. He means it for anyone, no exceptions named.
